Quick summary — how to participate in Boston tree‑removal (MGL 87) hearings

- Live/virtual testimony: Tree hearings are scheduled (generally) the first Thursday of each month at 10:00 a.m. and are held virtually. During the hearing the proponent presents, the Tree Warden describes the affected public shade tree(s), and the public may comment (raise your hand or use chat during the meeting). Public notices also list how to submit comments for each hearing. ([content.boston.gov](https://content.boston.gov/departments/parks-and-recreation/how-request-tree-removal-hearing?utm_source=openai))  
- What to include in written testimony: identify the hearing (neighborhood/address or “Tree Hearing – [date]”), say whether you support or oppose the removal and why (impact on canopy, safety, construction alternatives, replacement tree suggestions), and include your name and address so the record is clear. (If you want, I can draft a short testimony you can send.) ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/parks-and-recreation/participate-public-tree-ordinance-process?utm_source=openai))  
- Deadlines and decisions: Notices for tree hearings are posted (and posted on impacted trees) at least 7 days before the hearing. Final decisions are typically made within about two weeks of the hearing. Check the Public Notices page for the specific Aug. 6 items. ([content.boston.gov](https://content.boston.gov/departments/parks-and-recreation/how-request-tree-removal-hearing?utm_source=openai))

If you want me to:
- Find the specific Aug. 6 public notice(s) (project address + hearing link), say which neighborhood or give the project address; or
- Draft a 2–3 sentence or a 1‑minute live testimony script you can read at the hearing;

tell me which and I’ll fetch the exact public‑notice page(s) and prepare the text.

answer:
Yes, you can testify at the Tree Removal Hearing scheduled for August 6th. You have two options for participation: you can provide live or virtual testimony during the hearing, which starts at 10:00 a.m., by raising your hand or using the chat function. Alternatively, if you prefer, you can submit written testimony in advance via email to trees@boston.gov (with "Tree hearing" in the subject line) or by mail to the Tree Warden at the Boston Parks & Recreation Department.

When submitting testimony, be sure to specify the date of the hearing, state your position on the removal, and include your name and address for record-keeping. If you need further information or help with crafting your testimony, feel free to ask!

question: How do I apply for a business certificate through the city?

input.input: apply for business certificate City of Boston

tool_calls.output:
I can help — here’s what you need to do to apply for a City of Boston business certificate (DBA):

Summary steps
- Prepare your application: business name & address, names/addresses of owners/parties with interest, and a signed lease (or a notarized landlord letter if no lease). You cannot use a PO Box or virtual address for the business location. ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-clerk/how-apply-business-certificate?utm_source=openai))  
- Complete and print the City of Boston business certificate form and check “new filing.” The owner’s signature must be notarized (the City Clerk can notarize your signature if you bring a valid photo ID). ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2025/03/2025-New-Business-Certificate-Form_0.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- Include any additional documents required for your business type (examples: food trucks, restaurants, short‑term rentals, daycare, livery, home‑improvement contractors — see the City Clerk page for specifics). ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-clerk/how-apply-business-certificate?utm_source=openai))  
- Pay the filing fee: $65 (plus an additional $35 if you are not a Massachusetts resident). Business certificates must be renewed every four years; late renewal penalties apply. ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-clerk/city-clerk-services?utm_source=openai))

How to submit
- In person: City Clerk’s Office, Room 601, 1 City Hall Square, Boston, MA 02201. Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Bring your completed form, required documents, payment, and photo ID. ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-clerk/how-apply-business-certificate?utm_source=openai))  
- By mail: Include the completed form, payment, and a self‑addressed stamped envelope to: Office of the City Clerk, 1 City Hall Square, Room 601, Boston, MA 02201. ([boston.gov](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-clerk/how-apply-business-certificate?utm_source=openai))

Forms and help

answer:
To apply for a business certificate (DBA) in the City of Boston, you will need to follow several steps. First, prepare your application by collecting your business name, address, and the names and addresses of owners. Be sure to have a signed lease or a notarized letter from your landlord, as you cannot use a PO Box or virtual address. Next, download and complete the [City of Boston business certificate application form](https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2025/03/2025-New-Business-Certificate-Form_0.pdf), ensuring you check the "new filing" box. The owner's signature must be notarized, which can be done by the City Clerk with a valid photo ID.

You can submit your application either in person at the City Clerk’s Office or by mail. For in-person submissions, visit the office at Room 601, 1 City Hall Square, Boston, MA 02201, during business hours (Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.), bringing your completed form, required documents, payment of $65 (plus $35 if you're not a Massachusetts resident), and a photo ID. For submissions by mail, send your materials to the same address, including a self-addressed stamped envelope for your certificate. If you have further questions, you can contact the City Clerk at 617-635-4601 or the Office of Small Business Development at 617-635-0355.
